use_case_name: Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks

evidence_cards.content: Track reporting criteria are based on the requirements for the exchange of surveillance information and data usable in providing threat warning information among systems involved in joint operations.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence defines the high-level objective (goal) of the track reporting process, which is to provide threat warning information through data exchange in joint operations.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall accept all defined field values for retransmission and operator appreciation in the event of assuming R^2 for a previously-reported track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the specific objective of the actor (C2 JU) regarding the acceptance and processing of data fields for tracks, which constitutes the goal of this interaction.

evidence_cards.content: The exchange of Air, Surface (Maritime), and Land (Ground) surveillance information on the interface requires procedures to recognize and resolve

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.15 INFORMATION DIFFERENCE RECOGNITION AND RESOLUTION, first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly states the high-level objective for handling surveillance track data — recognizing and resolving differences in exchanged information — which directly defines the goal of publishing tracks in a coordinated C2 environment.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU shall transmit air, surface, or land tracks after achieving Active status and performing sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective of the use case: transmitting surveillance tracks under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: The recognition and resolution of dual designations require all IUs to periodically compare remote tracks to local tracks (and, optionally, to common local tracks) to determine if a dual designation has occurred.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the high-level objective for the system regarding track management, which is the goal of the use case.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have correlated local sensor data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit condition stated ('when:') that must hold for the C2 JU to assume reporting responsibility (R^2) and report the track, serving as a prerequisite state for the publishing action.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have the capability to originate and report real-time air, surface (maritime), land (ground), or space tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is a mandatory system capability that must exist before the C2 JU can perform common tracking and publish surveillance tracks as defined in the use case.

evidence_cards.content: All C2 JUs that originate real-time air or surface tracks shall have an automatic correlation capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Possession of automatic correlation capability is a required precondition for the C2 JU to prevent or eliminate dual designations during the track publishing process.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU must have initially achieved Active status, or returned to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the required system state (Active) and valid transitions (from Inactive/TDS Failure) that must exist before the use case of transmitting tracks can begin.

evidence_cards.content: Sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration must be performed before transmitting tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies specific procedural preconditions (checks, correlation, registration) that must be completed prior to transmission.

evidence_cards.content: Each C2 JU has the responsibility to determine whether the data points being detected by its local sensors are currently reported on the interface and if there are any conflicts between locally derived information and information reported on the interface.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes that before publishing tracks (the use case), the C2 JU must have already performed correlation checks between local sensor data and interface-reported data to identify conflicts. This is a prerequisite condition for the system state prior to track publication.

evidence_cards.content: To accomplish this, each C2 JU must continuously correlate locally derived ballistic missile tracks with ballistic missile tracks reported on the Surveillance NPG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that continuous correlation of local ballistic missile tracks with Surveillance NPG tracks is an ongoing requirement that must be in place before the C2 JU can proceed with reporting uncorrelated tracks or resolving conflicts — thus forming part of the preconditions for track publication.

evidence_cards.content: When a C2 JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence describes the trigger condition and initial action taken by the C2 JU in response to recognizing eligible tracks. While it is primarily relevant to the 'trigger' slot, it implies that the system must be in a state where tracks are already being reported to the interface (a precondition). However, per strict instructions, this specific claim belongs to the 'trigger' slot, not 'preconditions'. No explicit preconditions (system states that must hold *before* the use case begins) are defined on this page.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is the event where local/remote data held indicates that any of the specified correlation restriction conditions exist (e.g., Identity difference conflict, different Mode II codes, both tracks locally derived real-time, or Strength field > 1).
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific system state changes (data conditions) that initiate the restriction logic described in this section.

evidence_cards.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (receipt of J2/J3 message) that triggers the automatic decorrelation process required for track management prior to publication.

evidence_cards.content: A JU assumes R² if it has not received a remote report on a locally held Air or Surface (Maritime) track for approximately 40 seconds, or on a locally held Land (Ground) track for approximately 120 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the time-based trigger condition under which a C2 JU initiates responsibility assumption (R²), which is a prerequisite step before publishing tracks — thus indirectly defining when the publish use case may be triggered following this state change.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message on a locally held track shall assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an explicit event-driven trigger (receipt of J7.0 ACT=0 message) that causes the JU to assume R² and prepare to transmit — directly initiating the track publication use case upon meeting conditions.

evidence_cards.content: A JU without R² for a nonreal-time track with the TQ field set to value 0 shall assume R² for that track when the track is locally updated by a new nonreal-time report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a data-update-triggered condition (local update of nonreal-time track with TQ=0) that triggers R² assumption and subsequent transmission eligibility — serving as a trigger for the publish use case in nonreal-time contexts.

evidence_cards.content: A JU receiving a J2 PPLI message (with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive, Conditional Radio Silence, or TDS Failure) from a JU that has R² of a locally held track, may assume R² at the next opportunity to transmit the track if local reporting eligibility remains and a remote report has not been received on that track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes a conditional trigger based on receipt of specific J2 PPLI messages indicating peer status changes, enabling the receiving JU to assume R² and initiate track publication — relevant for fault-tolerant or degraded-mode triggering scenarios.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU transmits air, surface, or land tracks after initially achieving Active status, or after returning to Active status from Inactive status or TDS Failure.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific state transitions (achieving Active status) that trigger the transmission of tracks, serving as the start event for the use case.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks which are being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes an event (recognition of track eligibility) that triggers an action by the primary actor (C² JU), which is relevant to identifying potential trigger events for use cases involving track management and resolution.

evidence_cards.content: A J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit trigger event that starts the use case of publishing air and surface surveillance tracks when correlation fails due to message timeout.

evidence_cards.content: A J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit trigger event that starts the use case of publishing air and surface surveillance tracks when status indicators change to inactive or conditional silence.

evidence_cards.content: A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit trigger event that starts the use case of publishing air and surface surveillance tracks when a drop track command is received.

evidence_cards.content: The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is an explicit trigger event that starts the use case of publishing air and surface surveillance tracks when position quality degrades to zero.

evidence_cards.content: C2 JUs that have the capability to automatically initiate tracks for release to the interface without operator action shall also have the capability to deactivate this automatic capability.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies 'automatic initiation' as a specific trigger event for track publication (releasing tracks to the interface) in addition to manual actions implied by the general rules.

evidence_cards.content: The decorrelation process (and subsequent track handling) is triggered upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific external event (message receipt) that initiates the processing logic for tracks, serving as the trigger for the use case's internal flow.

evidence_cards.content: The transmission of air and surface tracks is triggered automatically or manually after the minimum wait period (12 seconds for air/surface) following the achievement of Active status and completion of checks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific events (time expiration, manual action) that initiate the track publication use case after preconditions are met.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for initiating action to resolve dual designations is when a C² JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This identifies the specific event (recognition of correlatable tracks) that starts the use case flow described in this section, which involves transmitting messages and resolving track conflicts — directly matching the 'trigger' slot definition.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU shall assume R² of an IU (including C² and nonC² JUs and forwarded PUs and RUs) in accordance with the reporting rules for a real-time track if the C² JU has correlated local sensor data, when: a. A J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, or b. A J2 PPLI message, other than J2.0, is received with the NPS Indicator set to Inactive or Conditional Radio Silence, or c. A J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is received from the FJU for a PU, RU, or other IU, or d. The Geodetic Position Quality in the J2 PPLI message is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section explicitly defines the specific events (triggers) that cause the C² JU to assume reporting responsibility and initiate track publication for inactive or limited status interface units, directly fulfilling the 'trigger' slot requirement.

evidence_cards.content: The correlation process commences with comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface.

source_locations.location: Section 4.4.4.3.1 AIR AND SURFACE TRACK CORRELATION

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This sentence explicitly defines the triggering event ('commences') for the track correlation use case, which is a prerequisite step for the 'Publish Air and Surface Surveillance Tracks' goal identified in prior slots.

evidence_cards.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines the explicit trigger event — receipt of a J2 or J3 message — that initiates automatic decorrelation testing, which is part of the track publication workflow’s pre-transmission validation phase. While not directly triggering ‘publication’, it triggers a mandatory step that must complete before tracks can be published, thus serving as an operational trigger within the use case context.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the use case is the completion of sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration performed after the C2 JU achieves Active status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies the specific event (completion of checks) that allows the system to transition from a waiting state to transmitting tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The unit originating a J3.7 EW Fix, AOP, or LOB report always retains reporting responsibility.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific condition (origination of a report) that triggers the retention of reporting responsibility for the C2 JU.

evidence_cards.content: The trigger for the C2 JU to publish its own status and engagement data is the receipt of a J7.1 (ACT = 1) message containing their own TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This section explicitly defines the event that initiates the response (track/status publication) for the C2 JU regarding its own tracks.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU initiates action to resolve dual designations when it recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This describes a trigger event for an action initiated by the C2 JU in response to recognizing correlated tracks, which is relevant to understanding triggers for track-related use cases.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assuming R² of an IU reports it as a track or point on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This is the primary action in the main flow: publishing the track to the surveillance network after assuming reporting responsibility.

evidence_cards.content: The type of surveillance message will depend upon the Environment/Category of the IU being reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies that the published track’s message type is determined by the IU’s category — a key constraint in the main flow for correct formatting and routing.

evidence_cards.content: The Identity shall be reported as Friend.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Mandatory identity value for tracks published under this use case — defines a fixed attribute in the main flow output.

evidence_cards.content: The Track Number, Platform and Platform Activity values received in previous PPLI messages shall be reported.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Requires preservation and retransmission of previously received track metadata — part of the canonical success scenario for consistent track continuity.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator shall be reported as value 1, and shall be maintained if another C² JU assumes R² of the IU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines specific field values (value 1) for PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator in the published track, and mandates persistence across handoff — critical for interoperability and track stability in the main flow.

evidence_cards.content: The JU with R² shall report all IFF/SIF valid data locally held for that track in accordance with the transmit rules for the J3 messages.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the primary action for the C2 JU (with R²) in the main flow of publishing surveillance tracks.

evidence_cards.content: Validity of codes for established tracks is determined as either 'Valid Data' or 'No Data' based on specific criteria: 'No Data' is reported when no valid code is currently held (reported as zeroes), and 'Valid Data' requires reception from own sensors on two or more successive interrogations for Modes I, II, and III with the same value, one interrogation for Mode IV, manually entered codes, or codes accepted via the IFF/SIF Difference Resolution Matrix.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the logic and conditions required to determine the data status before transmission, which is a critical step in the interaction sequence.

evidence_cards.content: Any change in the IFF/SIF code values from a No Data status to Valid Data or changes from Valid Data to other Valid Data will be reported as occurring.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the event-driven nature of the reporting flow, indicating that updates are triggered by status changes.

evidence_cards.content: After initially achieving Active status or returning to it from Inactive/TDS Failure, the C² JU shall not transmit air, surface, or land tracks until sufficient reporting responsibility checks, correlation, and data registration are performed.

source_locations.location: Page 54 (last page of region), Section 4.4.4.17, first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the mandatory procedural steps that constitute the main flow immediately following the preconditions and before transmission: performing checks, correlation, and registration.

evidence_cards.content: The minimum wait before reporting air and surface tracks is 12 seconds.

source_locations.location: Page 54 (last page of region), Section 4.4.4.17, first paragraph

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a concrete time constraint within the main flow sequence for Air and Surface tracks specifically.

evidence_cards.content: Each C² JU shall report on all uncorrelated local ballistic missile tracks and shall assume R² for those tracks in accordance with the R² rules as specified in paragraph 4.4.6.15.

source_locations.location: paragraph starting 'Each C² JU has the responsibility...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a mandatory action step in the main flow where the actor assumes reporting responsibility (R²) for uncorrelated tracks before transmission, which is part of the canonical success scenario for publishing tracks.

evidence_cards.content: In the event of conflict, the C² JU shall resolve the difference by transmitting the appropriate J7 message, by operator procedure, or by voice coordination.

source_locations.location: paragraph starting 'Each C² JU has the responsibility...'

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the specific resolution mechanism required within the main flow when data conflicts are detected during the correlation process prior to publication.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, that JU shall initiate action, either automatically or manually, to resolve the dual designation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines the specific interaction step where the primary actor (C2 JU) initiates the resolution process upon recognizing a dual designation condition.

evidence_cards.content: The recognizing JU shall transmit the J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform a correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the concrete system action (transmitting J7.2 message) taken by the actor to effect the correlation.

evidence_cards.content: The receiving IUs shall accept the requested correlation unless certain prespecified conditions exist which require or allow the receiving IU to reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Details the expected system response from receiving units and introduces the conditional logic for acceptance or rejection.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which the C² JU has R², the J7.2 Correlation message shall be transmitted with the Response Value (RV) field set to value 1 (Reverse Correlation Not Acceptable), the Source TN as the Retained TN, and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN; the C² JU shall then cease reporting the track and transmit a J7.0 Drop Track message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path where a detected conflict results in dropping the redundant surveillance track rather than publishing it, diverging from the main flow of track transmission.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are different, the J7.2 (RV = 1) Correlation message shall be transmitted, identifying the Source TN as the Retained TN and the surveillance TN as the Dropped TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative flow for resolving dual designations between different units by retaining the PPLI track and dropping the local surveillance track.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is found with a track for which another C² JU has R² and the TNs are the same, the receiving JU shall accept the PPLI information into its database and disregard the J3 surveillance data, unless Geodetic Position Quality is set to value 0, in which case the surveillance track is accepted and the PPLI message discarded.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow for handling identical tracks where data fusion occurs instead of new track publication, with a specific exception condition based on position quality.

evidence_cards.content: A C² JU assumes R² of an Interface Unit (IU) if a J2 PPLI message is not received for 40 to 60 seconds, received with NPS Indicator set to Inactive/Conditional Radio Silence, a J7.0 Drop Track message is received, or Geodetic Position Quality is set to value 0.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies the trigger conditions and subsequent actions for an alternative flow where the C² JU takes over reporting responsibility for an inactive unit, diverging from standard sensor-initiated tracking.

evidence_cards.content: If a JU without R² desires that a specific point, line, or area be transmitted immediately without awaiting the next periodic update, it should transmit a J7.1 (ACT = 1) Data Update Request for the desired TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes an alternative successful path where a JU requests immediate data transmission instead of waiting for the standard periodic update cycle.

evidence_cards.content: Another JU may assume R² for an emergency point if a J7.0 (ACT = 0) message is received on an emergency point declaring the current unit inactive, or if no periodic update is received for three consecutive update intervals.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow for reporting responsibility transfer based on timeout or explicit drop messages, diverging from the standard active maintenance.

evidence_cards.content: Changes from a Valid Data value to a No Data status as a result of the clearing function (J7.5 (ACT = 0)) will not cause the transmission of a change report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This defines an alternative flow where the system state changes (Valid Data to No Data) but the main reporting action is suppressed, diverging from the standard change reporting rule.

evidence_cards.content: Tracks with Valid Data which subsequently fail to respond to interrogations shall not be changed to the No Data status unless a Clear action is taken.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: This specifies an exception/alternative condition for status transition; it prevents the automatic transition to 'No Data' upon interrogation failure, maintaining the current valid state instead.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may cease reporting a track without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message if it has relinquished R² to another JU.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the standard termination message is suppressed due to a specific hand-off condition.

evidence_cards.content: The C2 JU may cease reporting a track without transmitting a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message if that track becomes an Active IU on the network with the same TN.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow where the standard termination message is suppressed because the track status changes to Active IU.

evidence_cards.content: When the Environment/Category changes from SPACE TRK to AIR TRK, SURF TRK, SUB TRK, LAND TRK, or LAND PT, the original Track Number (TN) is retained (S), and the entity is reported in the appropriate J3.x surveillance message; if proposed by J7.0 (ACT=1), acceptance or rejection by the R² JU shall be by manual action, and data shall not change until after acceptance.

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-1, row 'SPACE TRK' under columns AIR TRK through LAND PT, and LEGEND for S = SAME TN

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines a legal alternative flow where track number continuity is preserved during ENV/CAT change — diverges from main flow step 5 (reporting previous PPLI metadata) by retaining TN instead of potentially assigning new one; includes mandatory operator intervention condition.

evidence_cards.content: When the Environment/Category changes from EW AOP (1) to any other category except itself, the original TN is retained (S); if changing to another EW AOP (1), it is marked N/A — indicating no valid transition within same category; if proposed via J7.0 (ACT=1), manual acceptance/rejection required before data update.

source_locations.location: Table 4.7-1, row 'EW AOP (1)' across all columns, and LEGEND for S = SAME TN

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies an alternative successful path where TN retention applies even for electronic warfare area-of-point entities, with explicit exclusion for intra-category transitions — modifies main flow step 5’s metadata reporting rule based on source/target categories.

evidence_cards.content: If an AOP is formed from a single fix, the same TN shall be retained; if formed from two or more fixes, a new TN shall be assigned — this constitutes a conditional alternative flow branching from main flow step 5 depending on formation method.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Provides a concrete decision point that alters the main flow’s TN reporting behavior (step 5) based on how the AOP was constructed — represents a legally permitted variant path with different outcomes.

evidence_cards.content: For ASW POINTS/POINT AMP with specific point types (7, 1, 2, 4, 5, 12), certain ENV/CAT transitions are allowed with TN retention (N(3)) or assignment (X otherwise); otherwise, such transitions are illegal — defines constrained alternative flows applicable only to specialized ASW data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Introduces domain-specific exceptions to standard ENV/CAT transition rules, creating alternative successful paths limited to ASW contexts — directly affects whether step 5 retains or reassigns TN based on point type semantics.

evidence_cards.content: For Data Report Type 4 (Datum), the same TN may be used by operator action — allowing discretionary TN retention despite potential ENV/CAT mismatch, constituting an operator-driven alternative flow diverging from automatic TN assignment logic in main flow step 5.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Permits human-in-the-loop override of automated TN handling rules, enabling a non-standard but successful publication path when datum-type reports are involved — modifies expected system behavior in step 5 under specific conditions.

evidence_cards.content: When a C² JU recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it shall initiate action (automatically or manually) to resolve the dual designation by transmitting a J7.2 Correlation message requesting all other C² IUs to perform correlation of the two tracks.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative successful path where track publication is preceded by resolution of dual designations via correlation request initiation, diverging from direct publication in main flow.

evidence_cards.content: Receiving IUs may reject the requested correlation or respond with a reverse correlation request if certain prespecified conditions exist; the originating JU indicates constraints against accepting reverse correlation via the RV field in the J7.2 message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes branching logic within the alternative flow where receiving IUs can alter the correlation outcome based on local conditions, affecting whether dual designation resolution proceeds as initially requested.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation request is rejected, the J7.2 message with RV field set to value 2 shall be transmitted to report the rejection; if RV=3, it indicates manual initiation and acceptance unless specific rejection conditions apply.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies response codes and outcomes within the alternative flow that determine whether correlation succeeds, fails, or requires manual intervention — all still-successful variants of resolving dual designation before track publication.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may originate a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message by operator action only to clear one or more modes on a specified track.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative path where the actor initiates a specific clearing message manually rather than following the standard automatic reporting flow.

evidence_cards.content: All JUs, upon receipt of the J7.5 (ACT = 0) message, shall automatically set the designated mode(s) for the specified track to the No Data status.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes the system response in this alternative flow, diverging from the main flow's data transmission to a 'No Data' state update.

evidence_cards.content: A JU with R², upon receiving or initiating a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message that results in no IFF/SIF data being held, shall not continue transmitting the periodic J3 message that includes the continuation word containing IFF/SIF data.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies a variation in behavior (stopping specific transmissions) triggered by the clearing message, representing a divergence from the main flow's periodic reporting.

evidence_cards.content: Any JU may change a local mode to a No Data status without transmitting a J7.5 (ACT = 0) message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies a silent alternative path where the status changes locally without the network communication required in the main flow or other alternatives.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur spontaneously as a result of the R² unit reporting a No Data status (value 0) for one or more modes in a required IFF/SIF Surveillance data report.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative path for track data publication triggered by a specific 'No Data' status report from the primary actor, diverging from standard periodic updates.

evidence_cards.content: Data updating can occur as a result of an operator action wherein the update request is transmitted in a J7.5 (ACT = 2) IFF/SIF Update Request message.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines an alternative flow initiated manually by an operator to force a data update, distinct from automatic triggers.

evidence_cards.content: If a correlation is not found, the C² JU shall integrate the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines system response to failed correlation — an exception condition that triggers integration rather than track publication or responsibility assumption.

evidence_cards.content: If J2 messages are not received subsequent to integrating a non-correlated PPLI and the receiving C² JU still has no local data, the C² JU assumes no responsibility for reporting the subject JU on the Surveillance Network PG.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies terminal exception outcome: explicit relinquishment of reporting responsibility when no follow-up data arrives after initial non-correlated integration.

evidence_cards.content: If the position or other data in a PPLI meet a system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data shall be decorrelated.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Identifies decorrelation as an exception trigger condition requiring special handling outside normal main flow.

evidence_cards.content: After decorrelation, the C² JU shall initiate a surveillance track report with locally held data using a new track number.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Describes recovery behavior following decorrelation exception — creates new track instead of continuing existing one.

evidence_cards.content: The PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field shall both be reported as No Statement after decorrelation.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies constrained field values mandated during exception recovery path post-decorrelation.

evidence_cards.content: C² JUs shall not automatically correlate two tracks if local/remote data held indicates any of the following conditions exist: (1) The two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict; (2) The two tracks have different Mode II codes, and the local Mode II code is current; (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data; (4) Either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1.

source_locations.location: paragraph g, Correlation Restrictions, items (1) through (4)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Defines explicit exception conditions that prevent automatic correlation during track publication use case, constituting error or unexpected condition handling paths for the C2 JU primary actor.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction on correlation when tracks have an Identity (ID) difference constituting a conflict, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies recovery mechanism (operator override) for exception condition involving ID conflicts, allowing manual continuation of correlation despite automatic restriction.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall have an initialization parameter and an operator selectable capability to inhibit the automatic restriction on correlation when tracks have different Mode II codes with local code current, subject to interface coordination and promulgation to all C² IUs.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Specifies recovery mechanism (operator override) for exception condition involving Mode II code mismatches, allowing manual continuation of correlation despite automatic restriction.

evidence_cards.content: In lieu of specific interface direction, all IUs will restrict automatic correlation by default for both Identity conflict and Mode II code mismatch exceptions.

source_locations.location: end of paragraphs g(1) and g(2)

evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Establishes default system behavior for exception handling — automatic correlation is blocked unless explicitly overridden via coordinated interface direction.

evidence_cards.content: Systems shall not inhibit correlation if either track has Strength set to No Statement, even if the other track has Strength > 1.
evidence_cards.slot_relevance: Clarifies boundary condition for Strength-based exception — prevents false positive inhibition when one track lacks strength declaration, ensuring correlation proceeds under defined ambiguity.
